title: Siyavush Plays Polo before Afrasiyab
recordTitle: "Siyavush Plays Polo before Afrasiyab", Folio 180v from the Shahnama (Book of Kings) of Shah Tahmasp
medium: Opaque watercolor, ink, silver, and gold on paper

image.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Arthur A. Houghton Jr., 1970
image.license: Public domain. Released under Creative Commons Zero (CC0) through the Met's Open Access program

altText: A Persian miniature painting of riders on horses playing polo with long mallets, while onlookers watch, painted in bright opaque colors with touches of gold and silver.

source.verifiedBy: Met Collection API object record: title, artist field (the poet), date, medium, country (Iran), public-domain flag, credit line, tags (Men, Playing, Sports, Horses), classification (Codices) and image URLs read from the record

context: A folio from the Shahnama (Book of Kings) made for Shah Tahmasp in Iran around 1525 to 1530. The artist field names the poet Firdausi; the record does not name the painter. Its title and tags describe a polo game with horses.

descriptions.k: Riders on horses play a game with long sticks. This game is called polo. It is a page from a very old book. Can you find the horses? Which rider looks the fastest?
descriptions.g12: This page from a book shows a polo game in Persia, long ago. Riders on horses hit a ball with long sticks. The painting is full of bright color and shiny gold and silver. Find the horses and the riders. How can you tell they are moving?
descriptions.g35: This painting illustrates a story from the Shahnama, the Book of Kings, a famous Persian epic poem by Firdausi. It was made for Shah Tahmasp around 1525 to 1530. In the scene, Siyavush plays polo before Afrasiyab. Polo is a game on horseback with long mallets. Look at the horses and the crowd. How does the painter show action and excitement in a game?
descriptions.g68: Painted for Shah Tahmasp in the early 1500s, this folio from the Shahnama shows the hero Siyavush playing polo before the king Afrasiyab. In the story, the game is a chance to show skill. The painter fills the page with bright color, gold and silver, and arranges horses, riders and onlookers to build movement. How does the composition show both action and order, and why might a ruler have wanted such a scene in a book?
descriptions.g910: This illustration from the Shahnama of Shah Tahmasp turns a sporting contest into a courtly spectacle. The artist field names the poet, not the painter, a reminder that royal manuscripts were products of workshops. Horses and riders create diagonals and curves against a flattened, jewel-like space of color, gold and silver. How does the composition combine narrative, display of skill and decorative richness, and what does it suggest about court values?
descriptions.g1112: Siyavush Plays Polo before Afrasiyab comes from one of the most celebrated royal manuscripts of the Persian epic. As an illustration it works on several levels: narrative moment, display of courtly sport and decorative surface. The record names the poet but not the painter, so questions of attribution and workshop collaboration need caution. How do composition, color and materials support competing readings of the folio as story, spectacle and statement of royal taste?

teacherNote.context: A folio from the Shahnama made for Shah Tahmasp in Iran around 1525 to 1530. Polo was a favorite sport of Persian courts. The artist field names the poet Firdausi, not the painter.
directions: Ask students to trace the main diagonals and explain how they create motion.
Have students compare how this painting and a Western sports scene show speed.
Invite students to tell the story of a game they know as a single illustrated page.
